summary: Nirupam Chakma works in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the International Buddhist College, where he was supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and earned her D.Phil. at Wolfson College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich in 2003, later holding a visiting fellowship at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who earned his doctorates at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo (Professor Emeritus 1981–1994), and Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) specialized in religious studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he taught at Tokyo Gakugei University, the University of Tsukuba (~1978–1990), and Kanagawa University (~1990–2000).
Noboru Ueda (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an attested post at the University of Tokyo in 1990 and served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama and others. He was a professor at Otani University (~1985–2015) and president of Otani Junior College (~2004–2010).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (attested 1962) under Yutaka Ochihara and held assistant professorships at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota (born 1969) is a scholar of Indology and history. He completed undergraduate and graduate degrees at the University of Tokyo and has been a faculty member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies since 2002, becoming professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a research student at Taisho University. He served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi (born 1932) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from ~1955 to 1959 and later served as an assistant professor there (attested 1972).

Tensho Miyazaki (born 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2010) and held research and teaching positions at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo.

Nobumi Iyanaga (born 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969), lectured at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003), and held a research contract at the EFEO Tokyo Centre (2008–2014).
Nobuo Otsuka (born 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (born 1960) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein (~1990–1999), and held professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (appointed 2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji (born 1936) is a Sinologist and philosopher educated at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He served as professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College (1998–1999), and director at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

Nobuyuki Watase (born 1941) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He earned his master's degree from Kyoto University (~1964–1966), taught as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1985–2007), and served as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).

Nobuyuki Yamagiwa (born 1963) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturing post at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and serves as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto (born 1940) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University (~1959–1970) under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki, later working there as an assistant, lecturer, and departmental appointee (~1993–2006).

Nora Kershaw Chadwick (1891–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. She studied at Newnham College (~1911–1914) and held posts at the University of St Andrews (~1914–1919) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).
